answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A inlet delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A signal check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A voyage penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 588 identities need 588 bonds of 67 tokens, 42332 dollars of hardware and 25 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
